Certain Federal agencies are authorized to borrow money from the Treasury, largely to finance direct loan programs. In addition, agencies such as the Bonneville Power Administration are authorized to borrow from the Treasury to finance capital projects. Treasury, in turn, finances these loans by selling Treasury securities to the public.
Chapter 31 of Title 31 of the United States Code allows the Secretary of Treasury to borrow money by issuing Treasury securities. The Secretary determines the terms and conditions of issue, conversion, maturity, payment, and interest rate. New issues of Treasury notes mature in 2 to 10 years. Bonds mature in more than 10 years from the issue date. Each outstanding marketable security is listed in the "Monthly Statement of the Public Debt of the United States." The information in this section of the "Treasury Bulletin" pertains only to marketable Treasury securities.
Resources of the fund include (a) Fund Balance, which is available to support adjustments to loan and investment subsidy costs, repay borrowing from Treasury for loans and investments and expenditures for administrative expenses in support of the CARES Act, (b) U.S. Government securities (dollar balances), (c) special drawing rights (SDRs), an international reserve asset created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), (d) foreign currency holdings and (e) Investments in Special Purposes Vehicles. Principal sources of revenue -- or cost -- for the fund are gains-- or losses -- on SDRs and foreign investments, and interest earned on U.S Government, foreign securities, and SDRs.
The basic forms of budget authority are appropriations, authority to borrow, contract authority, and authority to obligate and expend offsetting receipts and collections. The period of time during which Congress makes funds available may be specified as 1-year, multiple-year, or no-year. The available amount may be classified as either definite or indefinite; a specific amount or an unspecified amount can be made available. Authority also may be classified as current or permanent. Permanent authority requires no current action by Congress.

python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Data for Borrowing from the public - Federal securities (in millions)
# FY2016 to FY2024

values = {
    2016: 1419286,
    2017: 666472,
    2018: 1258348,
    2019: 1208690,
    2020: 4234396,
    2021: 1484000,
    2022: 2453245,
    2023: 2150233,
    2024: 2241060
}

# Calculate natural log of each value
logs = {year: math.log(value) for year, value in values.items()}

print("Original values (millions):")
for year in sorted(values.keys()):
    print(f"  FY{year}: {values[year]:,} (ln = {logs[year]:.6f})")

# Sort the log values for trimming
log_values = sorted(logs.values())
print("\nLog values sorted:")
for i, v in enumerate(log_values):
    print(f"  {i+1}: {v:.6f}")

# 20% trimmed mean
# For 9 values, 20% = 1.8 values, so we trim 1 from each end
n = len(log_values)
trim_count = int(n * 0.20)
print(f"\nn = {n}, trim_count = {trim_count}")

# Trim from both ends
trimmed = log_values[trim_count:n-trim_count]
print(f"Trimmed values ({len(trimmed)} values):")
for v in trimmed:
    print(f"  {v:.6f}")

# Calculate mean of trimmed values
trimmed_mean = sum(trimmed) / len(trimmed)
print(f"\n20% trimmed mean of ln values: {trimmed_mean:.6f}")

# Round to nearest thousandths
rounded = round(trimmed_mean, 3)
print(f"Rounded to thousandths: {rounded}")

# For reference, show what this represents in original scale
print(f"\nIn original scale (millions): {math.exp(rounded):,.2f}")
EOF
